text: Republic Act No. 12009, the New Government Procurement Act signed on July 20, 2024, expressly repealed which earlier law?
optionA: RA 6713, the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees
optionB: RA 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act
optionC: RA 11032, the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act
optionD: RA 9485, the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act, signed July 20, 2024) is the procurement law; its repealing clause (Sec. 115) expressly repeals RA 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act of 2003.
hint: Think of the law the new act was written to replace, the one that used to govern bidding.
whyA: RA 6713 is the ethics code for public servants; it was not repealed by the procurement law.
whyC: RA 11032 covers red tape and processing time in government transactions, not procurement, and it remains in force.
whyD: RA 9485 was already amended by RA 11032 in 2018; it was never the procurement law.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act, pinirmahan noong July 20, 2024) na ang batas sa government procurement. Sa Sec. 115 nito, ni-repeal nito ang RA 9184 o Government Procurement Reform Act.
hintTl: Isipin mo kung anong lumang batas ang dating sinusunod sa bidding ng gobyerno.

text: Which law signed in November 2024 declares the Philippines' internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial sea, contiguous zone, exclusive economic zone, and continental shelf in line with UNCLOS?
optionA: Philippine Archipelagic Sea Lanes Act
optionB: Philippine Baselines Law
optionD: Philippine Fisheries Code, as amended
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12064, the Philippine Maritime Zones Act signed on November 8, 2024, defines the country's maritime zones (e.g., 12-nautical-mile territorial sea, 24-nautical-mile contiguous zone, EEZ, continental shelf) consistent with UNCLOS.
hint: The answer's name literally describes the areas being declared.
whyA: The Archipelagic Sea Lanes Act (RA 12065), signed the same day, designates routes for foreign ships and aircraft; it does not declare the maritime zones.
whyB: The Baselines Law is an earlier law that draws the baselines from which zones are measured; it is not the 2024 law that declares the zones.
whyD: The Fisheries Code governs fisheries and aquatic resources; it does not declare maritime zones.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12064 o Philippine Maritime Zones Act (pinirmahan November 8, 2024) ang nagde-declare ng maritime zones natin, gaya ng territorial sea, contiguous zone, EEZ at continental shelf, ayon sa UNCLOS.
hintTl: Yung pangalan mismo ng batas, sinasabi na kung ano ang dine-declare.

text: How many archipelagic sea lanes, with corresponding air routes, are designated by the Philippine Archipelagic Sea Lanes Act (RA 12065) of 2024?
optionA: Three
optionB: Two
optionD: Five
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12065 (signed November 8, 2024) designates three archipelagic sea lanes and their air routes through Philippine archipelagic waters for foreign ships and aircraft, per reports on the signing (Inquirer, Philstar).
hint: The lanes cut across the archipelago roughly north to south; count fewer than four.
whyB: Two is too few; the law names three lanes.
whyC: Four is more than what the law designates.
whyD: Five is more than what the law designates.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12065 (pinirmahan November 8, 2024) ay nag-designate ng tatlong archipelagic sea lanes kasama ang air routes nito para sa foreign ships at aircraft.
hintTl: Mas kaunti sa apat ang sea lanes na itinakda ng batas.

text: Under the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act (AFASA) of 2024, a person who knowingly lets his or her bank or e-wallet account be used to receive and transfer proceeds of scams is punished as a:
optionA: Social engineering scheme operator
optionB: Mass mailer
optionD: Money mule
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12010 (AFASA, signed July 20, 2024), Sec. 4(a), penalizes as a money mule anyone who uses, lends, buys, rents, or sells a financial account to receive, transfer, or withdraw proceeds of crimes or scams.
hint: The term compares the person to an animal that carries loads for others.
whyA: A social engineering scheme is obtaining confidential information through deception (Sec. 4(b)), not lending one's account.
whyB: A mass mailer is a tool that sends messages to 50 or more recipients; it is a circumstance that makes the offense economic sabotage, not the name of the offender.
whyC: Account takeover means getting into someone else's account; lending your own account is a different act.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 12010 o AFASA (pinirmahan July 20, 2024), Sec. 4(a), money mule ang tawag sa nagpapagamit, nagpapahiram, bumibili o nagbebenta ng account para tumanggap o maglipat ng pera galing sa scam.
hintTl: Hayop na tagabuhat ng karga ng iba ang pinagkunan ng term.

text: Republic Act No. 12023, signed on October 2, 2024, subjects digital services supplied by nonresident digital service providers (such as streaming platforms) and consumed in the Philippines to:
optionA: A 5% percentage tax on gross receipts
optionB: The 12% value-added tax
optionD: A 10% excise tax on digital content
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12023 (signed October 2, 2024) amended the Tax Code so that digital services, whether by resident or nonresident providers, are subject to 12% VAT; nonresident providers must register with the BIR (implemented by RR No. 3-2025).
hint: It is the same consumption tax already on most goods and services in the country.
whyA: The law did not create a percentage tax; it brought digital services under VAT.
whyC: No separate digital services tax was created; the law used the existing VAT system.
whyD: Excise taxes apply to specific goods like alcohol and tobacco, not to digital services under this law.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, dahil sa RA 12023 (pinirmahan October 2, 2024), ang digital services ng foreign providers na ginagamit dito sa Pilipinas ay may 12% VAT na, at kailangan nilang mag-register sa BIR.
hintTl: Parehong tax na nakapatong na sa karamihan ng binibili natin.

text: Republic Act No. 12021, signed on September 23, 2024 to protect the rights and welfare of domestic and overseas Filipino seafarers, is known as the:
optionA: Magna Carta of Filipino Seafarers
optionB: Philippine Maritime Labor Act
optionD: Overseas Seafarers' Rights Act
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12021 (signed September 23, 2024) is the Magna Carta of Filipino Seafarers, covering seafarers' rights, welfare, grievance system, and reintegration; MARINA issued its IRR.
hint: Its title borrows the name of a famous 13th-century English charter of rights.
whyB: No law with this title was enacted; it is an invented name.
whyC: This sounds plausible but is not the official short title of RA 12021.
whyD: The law covers both domestic and overseas seafarers, and this is not its title.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12021 (pinirmahan September 23, 2024) ay ang Magna Carta of Filipino Seafarers, para sa karapatan at welfare ng mga Pinoy seafarer, local man o abroad.
hintTl: Hiniram ang pangalan sa sikat na charter ng England noong 1215.

text: Under the Expanded Centenarians Act of 2024 (RA 11982), Filipinos receive a P10,000 cash gift upon reaching which ages?
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 11982 (signed February 26, 2024) amended the Centenarians Act of 2016 to give P10,000 at ages 80, 85, 90, and 95, while keeping the P100,000 gift at age 100.
hint: It starts at octogenarians and goes every five years until just before 100.
whyA: These ages are not covered; the law starts at 80.
whyB: The intervals are every five years, not ten, and 70 is not included.
whyD: The law starts at 80, and 99 is not one of the milestone ages.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 11982 (pinirmahan February 26, 2024), may P10,000 cash gift pagdating ng 80, 85, 90 at 95 years old, at P100,000 pa rin pag umabot ng 100.
hintTl: Nagsisimula sa 80, tapos every five years.

text: Under the No Permit, No Exam Prohibition Act (RA 11984), a student's status as 'disadvantaged' must be certified by:
optionA: The school registrar or guidance counselor
optionB: The barangay captain where the student resides
optionC: The DepEd schools division superintendent or CHED regional director
optionD: The local social welfare and development officer or the DSWD regional office
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 11984 (approved March 11, 2024), Sec. 4, requires certification by a municipal, city, or provincial social welfare and development officer or the DSWD regional office before covered schools must let the student take exams despite unpaid fees.
hint: The certifier is the office that assesses families in crisis, not the school.
whyA: The school is the party being required to allow the exam; it does not certify the student's status.
whyB: The barangay captain is not named as a certifying authority under the law.
whyC: DepEd, CHED, and TESDA impose sanctions on violating schools; they do not certify disadvantaged status.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 11984 (approved March 11, 2024), Sec. 4, ang magse-certify na disadvantaged ang estudyante ay ang MSWDO, CSWDO o PSWDO, o ang DSWD regional office.
hintTl: Hindi school ang nagse-certify; yung opisinang tumutulong sa pamilyang nasa crisis.

text: Aside from Negros Occidental (including Bacolod City) and Negros Oriental, which province is part of the Negros Island Region created by RA 12000 in 2024?
optionA: Guimaras
optionB: Siquijor
optionD: Antique
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12000 (Negros Island Region Act, signed June 13, 2024) forms the NIR from Negros Occidental with Bacolod City, Negros Oriental, and Siquijor.
hint: It is a small island province that was in Central Visayas, just off Negros Oriental.
whyA: Guimaras stays in Western Visayas; it is not part of the NIR.
whyD: Antique is on Panay and remains in Western Visayas.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 12000 (pinirmahan June 13, 2024), ang Negros Island Region ay binubuo ng Negros Occidental (kasama ang Bacolod), Negros Oriental at Siquijor.
hintTl: Maliit na island province malapit sa Negros Oriental.

text: Under RA 12027, which lapsed into law in October 2024, the primary media of instruction from Kindergarten to Grade 3 generally revert to:
optionA: Filipino and English, with regional languages as auxiliary media
optionB: The learners' mother tongue in all public schools
optionC: English only, to improve international test scores
optionD: The dominant regional language, with Filipino as auxiliary
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12027 (lapsed into law October 10, 2024) discontinued the mother tongue as the main medium of instruction in K to 3; Filipino and English are used, regional languages serve as auxiliary media, and mother tongue stays optional only in monolingual classes.
hint: The law moved away from the policy that used each child's home language.
whyB: That was the old MTB-MLE policy that RA 12027 discontinued as the default.
whyC: The law did not make English the sole medium; Filipino is also used.
whyD: Regional languages are only auxiliary under the law, not the primary medium.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, dahil sa RA 12027 (nag-lapse into law October 10, 2024), Filipino at English na ulit ang medium of instruction sa K to 3, at auxiliary na lang ang regional languages.
hintTl: Tinanggal ng batas ang mother tongue bilang main na gamit sa pagtuturo.

text: The Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program Act, RA 12028 of 2024, establishes:
optionA: Free tuition in state universities and colleges
optionB: An alternative learning system for out-of-school youth and adults
optionC: A national learning intervention and tutorial program for learners below minimum proficiency
optionD: A daily school-based feeding program for undernourished learners
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12028 (dated October 16, 2024) sets up DepEd's ARAL Program of tutorial sessions in reading, mathematics, and science for learners below minimum proficiency, using teachers, para-teachers, and pre-service teachers as tutors.
hint: The acronym itself is the Filipino word for 'study'; think of catching up on learning gaps.
whyA: Free tuition in SUCs comes from a separate free higher education law, not the ARAL law.
whyB: The Alternative Learning System is governed by its own separate law, not RA 12028.
whyD: School-based feeding is under a separate feeding-program law, not RA 12028.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12028 o ARAL Program Act ay nag-establish ng national tutorial program ng DepEd sa reading, math at science para sa mga learner na below minimum proficiency.
hintTl: Ang acronym mismo, salitang Filipino na ibig sabihin ay mag-study.

text: Republic Act No. 11996, known as the 'Eddie Garcia Law' signed in May 2024, primarily protects:
optionA: National Artists and their surviving heirs
optionB: Professional athletes in national sports events
optionD: Workers in the movie and television industry
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 11996 (signed May 24, 2024) sets work hours, written contracts, wages, social protection, and safety standards for movie and television workers; it was named after actor Eddie Garcia, who died after an accident on a TV set in 2019.
hint: Recall the veteran actor it was named after and where his fatal accident happened.
whyA: National Artists' benefits come from separate laws and proclamations, not RA 11996.
whyB: The law does not cover athletes.
whyC: It covers film and TV production workers, not specifically journalists.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 11996 o Eddie Garcia Law (pinirmahan May 24, 2024) ay para protektahan ang mga worker sa movie at TV industry, gaya ng work hours, kontrata at safety sa set.
hintTl: Alalahanin kung saan naaksidente si Eddie Garcia noong 2019.

text: The Kabalikat sa Pagtuturo Act (RA 11997) of 2024 provides public school teachers with:
optionA: A P10,000 monthly salary increase
optionB: An annual teaching allowance raised to P10,000 and exempt from income tax
optionD: A one-time service recognition incentive every five years
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 11997 (dated May 31, 2024; signed in ceremony June 3, 2024) institutionalized the teaching allowance for supplies, raising it from P5,000 to P10,000 starting SY 2025-2026, exempt from income tax.
hint: It is the yearly cash teachers use for chalk, paper, and classroom materials.
whyA: The law is about the teaching (supplies) allowance, not salary.
whyC: Housing loans are not part of this law.
whyD: The benefit is yearly, not a one-time incentive.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 11997 o Kabalikat sa Pagtuturo Act, ang teaching allowance ng public school teachers ay ginawang P10,000 kada taon simula SY 2025-2026, at tax-exempt pa.
hintTl: Pambili ng chalk, papel at gamit sa classroom.

text: Under the Civil Service Commission's 2025 Omnibus Rules on the Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), which earlier requirement was removed from the SALN?
optionA: Filing of the SALN every year
optionB: Filing of the SALN upon assumption of office
optionC: The signature of the declarant's spouse
optionD: Disclosure of liabilities
explanation: As of November 2026, the CSC Omnibus Rules on SALN (CSC MC No. 14, s. 2025; applying from 2026) removed the spouse's signature requirement, allowed digital filing and online oath-taking, and replaced CSC MC No. 2, s. 2013.
hint: The change involves a person other than the employee filing the form.
whyB: Filing upon assumption of office remains required under the rules.
whyD: Liabilities are still declared; it is part of the SALN's very name.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa bagong Omnibus Rules on SALN ng CSC (MC No. 14, s. 2025), hindi na kailangan ang pirma ng spouse sa SALN, at puwede na rin ang digital filing.
hintTl: May kinalaman sa ibang tao, hindi sa mismong empleyadong nagfa-file.

text: The Konektadong Pinoy Act, which lapsed into law in August 2025, allows data transmission industry participants to build and operate networks:
optionA: Without a legislative franchise, subject to registration with the National Telecommunications Commission
optionB: Only after obtaining a congressional franchise and a CPCN
optionD: Under licenses issued by local government units instead of the NTC
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12234 (Konektadong Pinoy Act, lapsed into law August 24, 2025) lets data transmission players set up networks without a legislative franchise, subject to registration with the NTC (Sec. 8).
hint: The law aimed to open the market to new players by removing a step that required Congress.
whyB: That was the old barrier the law removed for data transmission.
whyC: The law does not impose 100% Filipino ownership; foreign participation follows existing laws like the Foreign Investments Act and Public Service Act.
whyD: Registration is with the NTC, not with LGUs.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, dahil sa RA 12234 o Konektadong Pinoy Act (nag-lapse into law August 24, 2025), puwede nang mag-operate ang data transmission providers kahit walang legislative franchise, basta naka-register sa NTC.
hintTl: Tinanggal ng batas yung requirement na dumaan pa sa Congress.

text: Republic Act No. 12022 of 2024, which replaced the Anti-Agricultural Smuggling Act of 2016, mainly:
optionA: Sets mandatory price ceilings on rice and vegetables
optionB: Creates a separate Department of Fisheries
optionC: Replaces rice import quotas with tariffs
optionD: Treats large-scale smuggling, hoarding, profiteering, and cartels of agricultural and fishery products as economic sabotage
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12022 (Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act, signed September 26, 2024) repealed RA 10845 and penalizes smuggling, hoarding, profiteering, and cartels of agricultural and fishery products as economic sabotage, with a council chaired by the President.
hint: Look for the option that matches the 'economic sabotage' in the law's popular name.
whyA: Price ceilings fall under the Price Act, not RA 12022.
whyB: RA 12022 does not create a new department.
whyC: Rice tariffication was done by an earlier, separate law, not RA 12022.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa RA 12022 (pinirmahan September 26, 2024), ang malakihang smuggling, hoarding, profiteering at cartel ng agri at fishery products ay economic sabotage na, at ni-repeal nito ang RA 10845.
hintTl: Tingnan yung option na tugma sa salitang 'economic sabotage' sa pangalan ng batas.

text: The Anti-POGO Act of 2025 (RA 12312) repealed which law that had imposed taxes on offshore gaming operations?
optionA: RA 9487, extending the franchise of PAGCOR
optionC: RA 10927, covering casinos under the Anti-Money Laundering Act
optionD: RA 9287, increasing penalties for illegal numbers games
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12312 (signed October 23, 2025) bans offshore gaming operations and repeals RA 11590, the 2021 law that taxed POGOs, making permanent the ban under Executive Order No. 74 (2024).
hint: It is the newest of the four laws, passed in 2021.
whyA: RA 9487 concerns PAGCOR's franchise and was not the POGO tax law.
whyC: RA 10927 brought casinos under AMLA coverage; it is not the POGO tax law.
whyD: RA 9287 deals with illegal numbers games like jueteng.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12312 o Anti-POGO Act (pinirmahan October 23, 2025) ay nag-ban sa POGO at ni-repeal ang RA 11590, yung 2021 law na nagpataw ng tax sa POGO.
hintTl: Pinakabago sa apat na batas, 2021 pa lang ipinasa.

text: Which agency leads the implementation of the Free Funeral Services Act (RA 12309), which lapsed into law in 2025?
optionA: Department of Health
optionB: Department of the Interior and Local Government
optionC: Department of Social Welfare and Development
optionD: Philippine Health Insurance Corporation
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12309 (lapsed into law September 2025) provides free funeral services to poor families and families in crisis; the DSWD implements it, paying accredited funeral establishments through its AICS program.
hint: The same agency that gives burial aid to families in crisis.
whyA: DOH handles health services, not funeral assistance under this law.
whyB: DILG supervises LGUs but is not the lead agency for this law.
whyD: PhilHealth covers health insurance, not funeral services.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang DSWD ang nagpapatupad ng RA 12309 o Free Funeral Services Act, sa pamamagitan ng AICS program nila para sa mahihirap na pamilya.
hintTl: Yung ahensyang nagbibigay ng burial assistance sa mga pamilyang nasa crisis.

text: Under RA 12145 signed in April 2025, the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) was reorganized into the:
optionA: Department of Economy, Planning, and Development
optionB: Department of National Planning
optionD: Department of Economic Coordination and Development
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12145 (Economy, Planning, and Development Act, signed April 10, 2025) converted NEDA into the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) and reconstituted the NEDA Board as the Economy and Development Council.
hint: Its acronym is DEPDev.
whyB: No department with this name was created.
whyC: NEDA became an executive department, not a commission.
whyD: This is an invented name; the official name uses 'Economy, Planning, and Development'.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, dahil sa RA 12145 (pinirmahan April 10, 2025), naging Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) na ang NEDA.
hintTl: DEPDev ang acronym.

text: Which 2025 law authorizes the President to merge, restructure, or abolish redundant agencies of the Executive Branch and grants separation or retirement incentives to affected plantilla personnel?
optionA: Efficient Government Act
optionB: Executive Branch Reorganization Act
optionD: Public Sector Streamlining Act
explanation: As of November 2026, RA 12231, the Government Optimization Act signed on August 4, 2025, lets the President streamline Executive Branch agencies and GOCCs not under RA 10149, through a committee chaired by the Executive Secretary.
hint: The law's name is about making government work at its best, not about cutting.
whyA: No law by this name was enacted.
whyB: This describes what the law does but is not its title.
whyD: No law by this name was enacted.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang RA 12231 o Government Optimization Act (pinirmahan August 4, 2025) ang nagbibigay ng power sa President na i-streamline ang mga ahensya ng Executive Branch, may incentives pa sa maaapektuhang empleyado.
hintTl: Tungkol sa pagpapahusay ng gobyerno ang pangalan, hindi sa pagbabawas.

text: Under the CSC's Revised Dress Code for Government Officials and Employees (CSC MC No. 16, s. 2024), what attire is prescribed on the first Monday of each month?
optionA: Filipiniana-inspired attire
optionB: Agency-prescribed office uniform
optionD: ASEAN-inspired attire
explanation: As of November 2026, CSC MC No. 16, s. 2024 (CSC Resolution No. 2400766, August 29, 2024) prescribes ASEAN-inspired attire on the first Monday and Filipiniana-inspired attire on the second to fourth Mondays; it also allows attire matching one's gender identity and expression.
hint: The first Monday honors the country's regional neighbors.
whyA: Filipiniana-inspired attire is for the second to fourth Mondays.
whyB: Agency uniforms are for Tuesday to Friday.
whyC: Smart casual is for days without an agency-prescribed uniform.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa CSC MC No. 16, s. 2024, ASEAN-inspired attire ang suot tuwing first Monday ng buwan, at Filipiniana-inspired naman sa second hanggang fourth Monday.
hintTl: Para sa mga kapitbahay na bansa natin sa rehiyon ang first Monday.

text: In 2025, the Civil Service Commission amended the education requirements for first-level government positions to formally recognize:
optionA: Only holders of a bachelor's degree
optionB: Junior high school (Grade 10) and senior high school (Grade 12) completers under K to 12
optionC: Only applicants with at least two years of college
optionD: Only TESDA National Certificate II holders
explanation: As of November 2026, CSC MC No. 7, s. 2025 (CSC Resolution No. 2500229, March 6, 2025) recognizes K to 12 completers as meeting the education requirement for first-level positions, subject to other qualification standards such as eligibility.
hint: The change aligned civil service rules with the current basic education system.
whyA: A bachelor's degree is generally a second-level requirement, not the new first-level standard.
whyC: The amendment opened first-level posts to K to 12 completers, not only to those with college units.
whyD: TESDA certification was not made the sole education requirement.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa CSC MC No. 7, s. 2025, kinikilala na ang Grade 10 at Grade 12 completers para sa first-level positions sa gobyerno, basta pasok sa ibang qualification standards gaya ng eligibility.
hintTl: In-align ng CSC ang rules sa K to 12 system.

text: The 2025 Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service (2025 RACCS), promulgated by the CSC on April 30, 2025, replaced the:
optionA: 2017 Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service
optionB: 1999 Uniform Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service
optionC: 2011 Revised Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service
optionD: 2025 Omnibus Rules on Appointments and Other Human Resource Actions
explanation: As of November 2026, the 2025 RACCS (promulgated April 30, 2025, effective August 4, 2025) repealed and replaced the 2017 RACCS and added grave sexual harassment among offenses punishable by dismissal.
hint: Pick the most recent set of disciplinary rules before 2025.
whyB: The 1999 URACCS had long been superseded, first by the 2011 RRACCS.
whyC: The 2011 RRACCS was already replaced by the 2017 RACCS.
whyD: The Omnibus Rules on Appointments cover appointments, not administrative cases.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang 2025 RACCS ng CSC (promulgated April 30, 2025, effective August 4, 2025) ang pumalit sa 2017 RACCS, at isinama na ang grave sexual harassment sa mga offense na dismissal ang parusa.
hintTl: Piliin yung pinakahuling disciplinary rules bago mag-2025.

text: CSC Resolution No. 2600111, issued in January 2026, expanded the prohibition on gambling by government officials and employees to expressly cover:
optionA: Only gambling done during official working hours
optionB: Only unlicensed or illegal gambling houses
optionC: Online gambling such as online casinos, e-bingo, and e-sabong, even outside office hours
optionD: Only elective officials and their immediate families
explanation: As of November 2026, CSC Resolution No. 2600111 (January 19, 2026; published April 2026) bans government personnel from all forms of gambling, including online casinos, e-bingo, and e-sabong, and even mere presence in licensed casinos unless on official duty, during or beyond office hours.
hint: The update targeted gambling that can be done on a phone.
whyA: The ban applies during and beyond official working hours.
whyB: The ban covers licensed casinos too, not only illegal ones.
whyD: It covers officials and employees regardless of status across government, not only elective officials.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa CSC Resolution No. 2600111, bawal na sa government workers ang lahat ng sugal, kasama ang online casino, e-bingo at e-sabong, kahit labas na ng office hours.
hintTl: Yung sugal na kaya nang gawin sa cellphone ang dinagdag.

text: Under CSC Resolution No. 2600596, starting with the August 9, 2026 Career Service Examination, overseas Filipino workers may receive additional rating points if they have at least how many years of overseas employment?
optionA: Two years
optionB: Three years
optionD: Five years
explanation: As of November 2026, CSC Resolution No. 2600596 grants additional CSE rating points to OFWs with at least five years of overseas employment (continuous or intermittent, counted from January 1, 2000) who obtain a general rating of at least 70.00.
hint: It is half a decade of work abroad.
whyA: Two years is below the minimum set by the CSC.
whyB: Three years is below the minimum set by the CSC.
whyC: Ten years is more than what the CSC requires.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa CSC Resolution No. 2600596, may additional points sa CSE ang OFW na may at least five years na trabaho abroad, basta naka-70.00 man lang ang general rating.
hintTl: Kalahating dekada ng trabaho sa abroad.
